newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel wants to keep 25 pct of Telekom - report.
newsitem.headline: Waigel wants to keep 25 pct of Telekom - report.

text.p: Finance minister Theo Waigel wants the government to keep at least 25 percent of Deutsche Telekom despite possible plans to use Telekom share sales for budgetary purposes, the Berliner Morgenpost said on Thursday.

The newspaper said Waigel, together with coalition partners from Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU), believed the state should not give up all control of such important national infrastructure.
Such an intention would however open up a division in the government coalition, where junior partners the Free Democrats are urging that the state's entire remaining 75 percent stake be sold.
Waigel had said on Wednesday the government was considering selling part of its remaining stake in Deutsche Telekom earlier than the originally planned date of 2000.

The sale of Telekom shares is one possible measure for easing federal budgets that are looking increasingly stretched in the run-up to 1999 participation in the single European currency, which is based on 1997 economic data.
The Berliner Morgenpost said the government was above all anxious to ensure taxes did not have to be increased to make up a 1997 tax revenue shortfall estimated at close to 20 billion marks.

The newspaper said share sales in airline Deutsche Lufthansa AG and the sale of railway assets could raise up to two billion marks, while a spending freeze would save between two and three billion marks.
